title: AI Bill of Materials -- component declaration
description: One record: a system's intended component version, effective from a point in time. A full AI Bill of Materials is a list of these -- an append-only changelog, not a single 'current state' document. See ../schema/format.md for why each field is here.

system.description: The system this declaration applies to. Scoping is per-system: two systems can run different versions of the same component type without that being drift.

component_type.description: Exactly these four. A component type outside this set is a schema change, not a data entry -- it needs a deliberate update to the drift-detection query's category list, not a silent new value.

version.description: The human-readable version label (e.g. 'v2'). Mutable in the sense that two builds could carry the same label by mistake -- see `digest`.

digest.description: A content identifier for the deployed artifact. In production this is a real digest (sha256:<64 hex chars>) computed from the artifact itself; the synthetic examples in this repo use readable placeholder tokens after the 'sha256:' prefix instead of real hashes, so the worked example stays inspectable by eye. Exists because a version label is a claim, not a proof -- two different builds retagged with the same label look identical by `version` alone and only differ by digest.

effective_from.description: When this declaration became the intended state. There is no `effective_to` field -- it's derived as the next declaration's `effective_from` for the same (system, component_type), or 'still in effect' if there is none. Storing an explicit `effective_to` would let it drift out of sync with the next record's `effective_from`; deriving it can't.

declared_by.description: Who or what approved this declaration (a person, or an automated release process's identifier). A declaration nobody is accountable for is a config value, not governance evidence.

change_reason.description: Optional. Why this declaration superseded the previous one. Not required by the schema because not every declaration in a real system will have this filled in yet -- but its absence is itself something a reviewer should be able to see, not something the schema silently hides.
